images.filename: River Neath and Neath Canal at Ynysbwllog Aqueduct.JPG
images.caption: The Aquaduct carries the Neath Canal over the river Neath at Ynysbwllog, south of Resolven. The original aqueduct collapsed in 1979, and pipes carried the water across until the present steel aqueduct was completed in 2008, the largest single span aqueduct in the UK.

images.caption: The 10 arched Aberdulais Aqueduct carries the Tennant Canal over the River Neath to join the Neath Canal on the east side of the river, near the Aberdulais tin works. A railway bridge and road bridge can both be seen beyond the aqueduct. The river is shown in spate following heavy rain in early June 2012.

images.filename: Neath Abbey and the Tennant Canal.JPG
images.caption: The ruins of the cistercian Neath Abbey, alongside a section of the Tennant Canal, in the Neath valley. On the right of the ruins is a ruined 17th century mansion built within the abbey ruins. The site was heavily industrialised in the 19th C, excavated in the 1920s, is now in the care of Cadw.
